title: Vector endpoint stabilizer: microbatch controller + kernel fallback for p99 reduction
creator: Marco Liu
description:
Goal: Reduce tail latency (p99/p999) for the vector embeddings endpoint by combining a lightweight microbatch controller, smarter kernel selection heuristics, and a graceful quantized-kernel fallback path. This ticket coordinates design, infra changes, kernel hints, and telemetry so we can measurably cut p99 without increasing average cost by >10%.

Background: Over the last quarter we've seen intermittent p99 spikes on the embeddings endpoint during bursty ingress patterns. Profiling indicates three dominant causes: (1) inefficient microbatch coalescing under high variance of request sizes, (2) expensive kernel paths selected for small microbatches, and (3) occasional long-running stragglers due to memory-copy stalls on certain GPU configurations. Standalone experiments improved each area but we need an integrated, deployable stabilizer that works for multi-tenant traffic and preserves throughput goals.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce embeddings endpoint p99 latency by >= 25% on production-like traffic mix in the Canary region
No degradation in p50 and <=10% increase in token-cost per request on average
New telemetry dashboards showing per-kernel p99, microbatch sizes, and straggler rates are available
Graceful fallback to quantized-kernel path behaves within SLOs and is covered by e2e tests
tasks: Implement microbatch controller that maintains soft target batch window (configurable, default 8ms) and reactive flush on deadline or backlog
Add kernel-hint API to runtime: attach expected sequence-length and microbatch-size to dispatch requests
Implement speculative hedging: after 12ms of waiting for a microbatch to fill, spawn a quantized-kernel fallback for in-flight requests
Add ingress prewarm hook for hot tenants: predictive KV cache prefill based on recent traffic histogram
Create e2e perf harness to replay production ingress traces at 1x/10x scale for canary testing
Write unit/integration tests and a safety kill-switch config flag
measurement_plan: Baseline collection: 7 days of current p50/p95/p99/p999 from /metrics/vec-endpoint prior to rollout
Canary run: deploy to region-us-canary on 10% of traffic with simultaneous trace-level profiling
Compare per-kernel latencies, microbatch size distribution, and GPU utilization before/after
Run controlled replay with synthetic bursts (10k reqs/sec sustained for 2m) to validate tail behavior
Post-rollout: automated 24h regression check that reverts if p99 worsens by >5%
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag: embeddings.stabilizer.enabled
Phase 1: internal staging verification with 1–2 tenants (QA + infra) — 3 days
Phase 2: canary region (region-us-canary) at 10% traffic for 48h with close monitoring
Phase 3: ramp to 50% in 24h if canary metrics stable, then 100% in next 48h
Rollback: immediate disable of runtime flag triggers instant fallback to previous scheduler and kernel routing
risks_mitigation: Risk: Hedging spawns could double GPU kernel invocations under extreme tail — Mitigation: cap concurrent hedges per-GPU and use cheap quantized kernels first
Risk: Changes to microbatch timing could reduce throughput — Mitigation: tune target window by tenant tier and maintain autoscaling slack
Risk: Incorrect kernel hints could regress latency for some models — Mitigation: conservative default hints and model-level opt-out via config
Risk: Telemetry overload during canary — Mitigation: sampling at 10% and offloading heavy traces to debug-only buckets
